clue.text: Tomboy's "Enigma Variations"

indicators.note: variations on a theme rework the same material in new forms, so these letters get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the word from Elgar's title

explanation.surface: A tomboyish girl is apparently fond of Elgar's famous orchestral work.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted title looks like a piece of music; only its first word is fodder, and 'Variations' tells you what to do with it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamine is a slim, boyish girl with mischievous charm, close in sense to a tomboy.

clue.text: Article gives partial knowledge about something dangerous

parts.note: knowing only a bit of something

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece offers only a half-understanding of some hazard.
explanation.walkthrough: Pope wrote that a little learning is a dangerous thing, which is why the phrase is defined as something dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb from Alexander Pope calls shallow knowledge a dangerous thing, so the phrase itself names something hazardous.

clue.text: Guess it's a finer composition

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters are assembled afresh

explanation.surface: Someone judges a piece of music to be of higher quality.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to deduce or conclude from evidence, a reasoned kind of guessing.

clue.text: Flagrantly bad, for example, one grouse badly treated

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: something treated badly is knocked about out of its proper shape, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Mistreating a game bird is held up as an example of outrageous conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes in the I from 'one' as well as the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Egregious means outstandingly bad, shocking in its obviousness.

clue.text: Change oneself, creating another identity

explanation.surface: Reinventing yourself produces a second persona.
explanation.definitionFit: An alter ego is a second self or persona, Latin for 'other I'.

clue.text: Years putting state first is mean

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
an age is a long span of years

explanation.surface: A person who has been putting the nation first for years is called stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting state first' tells you the word for state goes before the word for years.
explanation.definitionFit: In statistics the mean is the arithmetic average of a set of values.

clue.text: Pasta's cooked for continental snacks

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Pasta is being prepared as a European light bite.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapas are small Spanish savoury dishes, snacks from mainland Europe.

clue.text: Managed old city firm first with bitterness

parts.note: ran a business means managed it
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city

explanation.surface: Someone ran an ancient city's company resentfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm first' puts the company abbreviation before the old city. Ur is the usual crossword old city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is deep-seated resentment, a lasting bitter feeling.

clue.text: "Duck and Pheasant" team with alliance make winning declaration

parts.note: both are game birds, wild animals hunted for food
a set is a group of people
a match is a union, as in marriage

explanation.surface: A team of two pub names joining forces sounds like a merger announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotes make 'Duck and Pheasant' look like a pub; together the two birds are simply game.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis umpires announce game, set and match when the final point wins the contest, so it declares victory.

clue.text: Wind strength affects service

explanation.surface: A strong gale disrupts a tennis serve or a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: The armed forces are called the services, and the air force is one branch of them.

clue.text: Criticise one mother in a hat

parts.note: critics pan a show they dislike
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a woman wearing a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A panama is a lightweight straw hat originally made in Ecuador.

clue.text: Disturbance in last irregular meeting

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow
the two following words meet, and the answer straddles the join between them

parts.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Trouble broke out at the latest disorderly gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A stir is a commotion or fuss, a disturbance of calm.

clue.text: Prison where plants are grown

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British military slang for a detention block
second meaning: a glass building for cultivating plants

explanation.walkthrough: In British army slang the glasshouse is a military prison, named after the glass roof of the old Aldershot detention centre.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a greenhouse for growing plants and, in army slang, a military jail.

clue.text: Information also found on penguin

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Facts also turn up in a Penguin paperback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penguin' suggests the publisher of paperbacks; here it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentoo is a species of penguin with a white stripe across its head.

clue.text: Regime at variance with move to another part of the world

definitions.text: move to another part of the world

indicators.note: things at variance disagree and differ, so the letters vary their order

explanation.surface: Someone at odds with the government decides to leave the country.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'at' of 'at variance' is part of the fodder, not the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to leave one's own country to settle in another.

clue.text: Fashionable brilliance that's clever …

parts.note: setter's reading: the word for fashionable placed before a word for brilliance, read as a loose phrase

explanation.surface: Stylish genius turns out to be smart, continuing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: IN (fashionable) + GENIUS (brilliance) gives INGENIUS, one O short of the answer, so the wordplay works only as a sound-alike pun rather than an exact charade.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingenious describes something cleverly inventive, showing original skill.

clue.text: Mental affliction that's new, they say, so Sir is confused

indicators.note: what people say is spoken, so this word is taken by its sound

parts.note: the first syllable of the answer is pronounced like this word

indicators.note: confused letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: A knight's freshly developed mental illness leaves him muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurosis is a mild mental disorder marked by anxiety or obsessive behaviour.

clue.text: … if right inmate changes into old-fashioned clothes

indicators.note: something that changes takes a new form, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a prisoner cleverly swaps into period costume.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an archaic word for clothing or garments.

clue.text: Salary — spend it maybe!

indicators.note: maybe signals a possible version of these words, letters reordered

explanation.surface: A pay packet comes with the advice to go out and use it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as a comment on what to do with your pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed regular payment, especially to a clergyman or student.

clue.text: Sneer returned to German in the party

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: A scornful look is given back to a German at the political gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greens are an environmentalist political party, active notably in Germany.

clue.text: Itch giving annoyance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sore, tickling sensation of the skin
second meaning: the state of being vexed

explanation.surface: An itch makes you cross.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both physical soreness of the skin and mental exasperation.

clue.text: Fool alien with something of value

parts.note: an ass is a foolish person

explanation.surface: An idiot from outer space turns out to be a treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful or valuable thing or quality.

clue.text: About wild mob executing search

indicators.note: something wild is unruly, so the letters run out of order

explanation.surface: An unruly crowd is carrying out a manhunt.
explanation.definitionFit: To comb an area is to search it thoroughly, as with the teeth of a comb.

clue.text: Arrived with nothing but secured a small role

explanation.surface: An actor turned up empty-handed yet landed a bit part.
explanation.definitionFit: A cameo is a brief appearance by a well-known actor in a film or play.

clue.text: Drive around with son to see aquatic performers

indicators.note: turning a word around in loose order lets its letters move

explanation.surface: A parent drives a son around to watch a diving display.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers perform underwater or off boards into a pool, so they are performers in water.

clue.text: Evil atrocity

explanation.walkthrough: The everyday sense of hugeness is a trap; the traditional sense is extreme wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormity strictly means outrageous wickedness or a grave crime, not merely large size.

clue.text: Data I get incorrectly, becoming nervous

indicators.note: something done incorrectly is wrong, so the letters come out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone receiving wrong figures grows anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitated describes being troubled, flustered and on edge.

clue.text: Calm, therefore surprisingly hot on one point

indicators.note: a surprising result is unexpected, so the letters land in an unexpected order

parts.note: E, east, is one of the compass points

explanation.surface: Someone is unexpectedly cool even when the heat is on.
explanation.definitionFit: To soothe is to calm someone, easing their pain or agitation.
